sessions.name: Friday Night Welcome Reception
sessions.description:
Join us at the beautiful and historic Tuthilltown Distillery, nestled in the heart of the Gunks for an amazing welcome evening reception: firepits, craft whiskey, a Mexican food truck, views of the mountains, affinity group meetups, craft vendors, and a special climbing slideshow.

Our keynote speaker will be Karsten Delap, Petzl athlete, IFMGA/UIAGM Licensed Mountain Guide, and owner of Pisgah Mountain School in North Carolina, and is coming to GunksFest to speak and lead a guest clinic this year!

Karsten is a passionate educator, well-known for his global resume of climbing and technical skills in the mountains.

His Friday night talk will center around safety and risk management in the world of trad climbing – custom-tailored to the GunksFest audience and sure to benefit any level of climber.

Come hungry, come thirsty, and come stoked to kick off GunksFest 2026 in style!

Plenty of parking is required, please plan on driving responsibly as our beautiful mountain roads have limited streetlights and plenty of wildlife.

Doors – 5pm
Slideshow 7pm
Arrive early for tastings, distillery tours, and disc golf! See tuthilltowndistillery.com for more info.
sessions.location: New Paltz, NY

sessions.name: Multipitch Strategies for Efficiency and Safety
sessions.rawName: Multipitch Strategies for Efficiency and Safety (Saturday 8am - 12pm)
sessions.description:
Guide: Angelo Urrico, Rise Outside guides

Join Rise Outside’s Angelo Urrico for an immersive 4hrs in getting your multi-pitch skills dialed.

Angelo will cover a variety of multi-pitch topics, including gear, anchoring, belays and belay transfers, rope management, swapping leads, and much more!.

Prerequisites: Previous outdoor rock climbing experience; a desire to multi-pitch climb
Required gear: Personal climbing kit, anchor gear and anchor material
sessions.location: Meet at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Yoga For Climbers - PreClimb Warm Up Class
sessions.rawName: Yoga For Climbers - PreClimb Warm Up Class (Saturday 8am - 8:45am)
sessions.description:
With: Laura Obringer

Kick GunksFest off with our favorite yoga instructor Laura as she gets you warm and limber for a weekend of climbing. A climber herself, Laura knows all the moves to get your body and mind prepped for the day.

Prepare yourself for a great day on the rock with a warm-up targeted specifically for climbing that blends traditional yoga with modern kinesiology. The class runs 40 minutes so that participants can be at their climbing clinics ontime. For more information, please visit www.laurayogaclimb.com

This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center and will be held on the covered patio.

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: Yoga mats will be provided
sessions.location: MP Visitor Center Covered Patio

sessions.name: Anchor Power: Advanced Anchoring for Women & Non-Binary
sessions.rawName: Anchor Power: Advanced Anchoring for Women & Non-Binary (Saturday 9am-4pm)
sessions.description:
With: Patty Lankhorst, Gunks Guides

Take your anchor skills to the next level. This hands-on clinic will explore more advanced anchor-building techniques, gear selection, and creative solutions for building solid, efficient systems in a variety of climbing situations. We’ll focus on the “why” behind anchor choices so you can make confident decisions when the perfect textbook anchor isn’t an option.

Note this clinic is only open to women and non-binary climbers.

Prerequisites: Some general anchor building knowledge using traditional gear will be helpful for this clinic

Required Gear: Personal gear and a trad rack if you have one
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Glacier Travel and Crevasse Rescue
sessions.description:
Guide: Gregory Kanter, Gunks Guides

This course made it's debut in 2025 and was a huge success! Bystanders watched as our fearless group of mountaineers made their way through the festival grounds clad in mountaineer's coils and dripping with mountain rescue hardware.

Take your climbing skills to the next level by building on the techniques used in rock climbing to explore new and thrilling terrain on glaciated peaks. In this Glacier Travel and Crevasse Rescue course, you will learn how to navigate glaciers and tackle challenging mountain environments.

Throughout the course, you’ll gain hands-on experience with the specialized gear needed for mountaineering, and how to properly use and move with it. Learn the critical skills for traveling on glaciers as part of a rope team, protecting snow climbs, and performing essential crevasse rescue techniques. Whether you’re rescuing a partner or yourself after a crevasse fall, this course will give you the skills and confidence to handle emergencies in high-mountain terrain.

This course is good for all levels. We will customize your day based on your experience level, ensuring you get the most out of the training no matter where you’re starting from. Available all year round, sign up today and unlock the door to new mountaineering adventures!

If you endeavor to spend time in the big mountains you won't find a better primer!

Prerequisites: A strong motivation for hands on learning and active participation! It will be helpful to have familiarity with basic climbing knots and hitches
Required Gear: Personal climbing gear plus any of the following that you have: Pulleys, locking carabiner, progress capture device, prussiks, slings. There will be some to use at the clinic too
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Not Your Typical CPR: Adult + Child CPR/AED for Climbers
sessions.rawName: Not Your Typical CPR: Adult + Child CPR/AED for Climbers (Saturday 9am-2pm)
sessions.description:
Instructors: Raquel Sapp + Brittany Leavitt, Backcountry Pulse

CERTIFICATION COURSE

CPR classes can feel clinical and disconnected from the places where emergencies actually happen. This one is built for climbers, and just may be the most important skill you ever bring to the crag.

In this hands-on course, participants will learn and practice rescuer psychological preparedness, adult and child CPR, AED use, choking care, and the early actions that can make a meaningful difference while help is on the way.

We will place those skills in situations that feel familiar to climbers: working in an outdoor setting, making use of the resources available, and figuring out what needs to happen next.

Participant Benefit: Certification - Everyone who completes the course and exam will receive a Backcountry Pulse Adult + Child CPR/AED certification!

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: None. Backcountry Pulse will provide CPR manikins, AED trainers, and course equipment
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Partner Rescue with Guest Guide Karsten Delap
sessions.rawName: Partner Rescue with Guest Guide Karsten Delap (Saturday 9am-1pm)
sessions.description:
Guide: Karsten Delap, Pisgah Climbing School

Join our 2026 guest keynote speaker and IFMGA guide Karsten Delap for an exclusive clinic on partner rescue.

With years of big mountain experience and trained to the highest certifications, Karsten will be on hand for this intensive course that all levels of climber will benefit from.

He will provide tools to set you up for success when things go wrong, and get you and your partner down safely in any situation.

Prerequisites: Motivation to step up and manage rescue situations in the vertical
Required Gear: Personal kit: prusik cord, ATC belay plate, gri-gri, cordellete, slings, etc.
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Ropecraft 101: Knots and hitches every climber should know
sessions.rawName: Ropecraft 101: Knots and hitches every climber should know (Saturday 9-11am)
sessions.description:
Guide: Dan Gorski, Rise Outside guides

As a climber, your most important tool is your rope! This clinic will teach you the essential knots and hitches needed to climb in the gunks, and where and how to implement them
Prerequisites: Beginner-intermediate focused
Required gear: None required, you are welcome to bring a rope/cordalette with which to practice
sessions.location: Meet at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Top Rope Anchors: Anchoring Fundamentals
sessions.description:
Guide: Eric Waldron, Gunks Guides

This top rope anchoring class is designed to help you gain the skills needed to get out climbing on your own.

Focusing on essential techniques like gear selection, guidebook interpretation, and natural anchor construction, this hands-on course provides the foundation for safe and efficient anchor setups. You’ll build practical experience in constructing reliable anchors while learning best practices.

This course also sets the stage for future advanced skills like learning to lead and gives you a better understanding of what’s happening when climbing with others. Perfect for climbers looking to gain independence and strengthen their technical abilities.

Prerequisites: Some previous outdoor climbing experience is helpful but not required
Required Gear: Personal climbing gear (ie. harness and helmet), Optional: bring your own ropes, static ropes, locking carabiners, slings, ATC-style belay device, ABD-style belay device (preferably a Grigri), several (up to 6) locking carabiners similar to Petzl Attaché, at least 1 double-length (48″ or 120 cm) sling, 2 shoulder-length (24″ or 60 cm) slings, other personal gear that you use or have questions about
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Trapps Bouldering Tour
sessions.description:
Join us for a walking tour of the boulders in the Trapps. Get oriented from the classics to hidden gems with an expert bouldering guide sponsored by Mustangs Climbing Gym in Kingston.

Please note this is a walking tour only, and not a guided climbing experience.
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve visitor center.

sessions.name: What Happens When Things Go Sideways
sessions.rawName: What Happens When Things Go Sideways (Saturday 9-11am)
sessions.description:
Guide: Alan Kline, Rise Outside guides

One of our longest-running and most popular masterclasses in Gunks literacy.

What happens if you drop your belay device? Or forget your harness? Or (gasp!) don't have enough snacks?!

The unforeseen happens all the time in this silly activity, and it's better to have a plan for the worse than be stuck.

Join Rise Outside guide Alan Kline for a dive into the nuanced and creative ways to solve problems.
Prerequisites: Helmet, Harness, Personal climbing gear
Required gear: A foundation in outdoor climbing
sessions.location: Meet at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: How to be a Good Second
sessions.rawName: How to be a Good Second (Saturday 10am - 12pm)
sessions.description:
Instructor: Richard Goldstone

We are very happy to be bringing this clinic back, as it's one of our most popular festival events.

From the technical to the theoretical, Gunks legend Richard Goldstone brings his legendary teaching style to this class - sure to pack the house.

We'll talk about personal gear, belaying, choss management, cleaning gear, belay transitions, rappelling, getting yourself out of jams, expedition mentality, and maybe just a touch about evaluating potential leaders.

This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center and will take place in the Visitor Center classroom.

Prerequisites: The intended audience for this clinic is climbers who are transitioning from gym or sport climbing to multipitch trad climbing and who want to know more about the skills involved in competent trad seconding
sessions.location: MP Visitor Center Classroom

sessions.name: Beyond the Onsight: Broadening your Trad Climbing Horizons
sessions.rawName: Beyond the Onsight: Broadening your Trad Climbing Horizons (Saturday 12pm-2pm)
sessions.description:
Guides: Alan Kline and Dan Gorski, Rise Outside guides

This clinic discusses the elements that go into working trad climbs in the gunks. We'll dive into choosing the climb for you, finding your beta, assessing gear, and centering your mindset as you begin pushing your limits.
Prerequisites: Experience leading on gear, confidence in gear assessment (intermediate-advanced focused)
Required gear: None required, you are welcome to bring any trad gear for discussion/demonstration
sessions.location: Meet at the afternoon clinic meeting location.

sessions.name: Mushroom Foraging
sessions.description:
Guide: Jannette Pazer, GCC

Do you love mushrooms? Have you always wanted to learn how to forage for mushrooms but were afraid to try? This clinic is meant for beginner foragers who what to learn how to identify wild mushrooms, as well as learning about some local edible mushrooms and some deadly ones as well.

Clinic will consist of a 1 hour presentation, then at least 1 hour of foraging and trying to identify our finds.

Note: we’re scheduled for 2 hours, but we can continue foraging for another hour for those who are interested.

Prerequisites: None
Required gear: Hiking gear - sturdy shoes, water and snacks
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Cams: From Soup to Nuts
sessions.description:
Instructor: Richard Goldstone

Along with being a groundbreaking Gunks climber, Richard Goldstone is among our most talented instructors, whose teaching style has captured audiences at previous GunksFests, mixing the anecdotal with the scientific, and this cam-focused session is no exception.

This clinic aims to discuss all aspects of cams. There’s a touch of history, a smidgen of theory, a review of failure modes, and some practical guidelines for placements. Richard will try to illuminate how not to do things as well as how to do them.

This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center and will be held in the visitor center classroom.

Prerequisites: None
Required gear: None
sessions.location: MP Visitor Center Classroom

sessions.name: Intro to Gunks Climbing
sessions.description:
Guide: Angelo Urrico, Rise Outside guides

This immersive clinic is geared towards the trad climber looking to expand their knowledge of gunks routes and history, with an explanation of all the Gunks climbing areas. Angelo will walk you through all you need to know to get up (and down) safely, as well as areas that are best on crowded days, best spots with easy leads to access harder TRs, and, of course, best swimming spots on hot days...

Participants will be introduced to the various Gunks cliffs, with special attention to the Trapps, including navigating the base, route-finding, decent options, and details of the most classic Gunks routes!

Prerequisites: None
Required gear: Proper hiking footwear, guidebook or Gunks app
sessions.location: Meet at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Antlion Tour
sessions.description:
Join us for a guided walking tour of the Antlion cliff. You'll be guided by Peter Cody, Chairman of the GCC and one of the cliff's developers with many first ascents to his name.

Pete will point out classics, hidden gems, routes with great protection, good for breaking into the grade routes, and notorious sandbags, as well as provide some history behind this wilderness crag.

Please note this tour requires a long uphill approach, approximately 1hr of hiking each way with significant elevation gain.

You will be responsible for setting up your own ropes, but time will be allotted for climbing.

Come prepared for a day of climbing: snacks, plenty of water, sturdy hiking shoes, and your full climbing kit!

This clinic departs from the Campground and will require personal transportation!
sessions.location: This clinic departs from the Campground and will require personal transportation!

sessions.name: Because Things Happen: Self Rescue
sessions.description:
Guide: Eric Waldron, Gunks Guides

Oh Crap! Now What?

Things don’t always go according to plan—but with the right skills, you can handle the unexpected. This hands-on clinic puts you in realistic climbing scenarios and challenges you to figure out what to do when things go sideways.

We’ll work through practical problem-solving skills for situations like stuck ropes, tricky rappels, unexpected partner issues, and other common climbing curveballs.

Come ready to think, experiment, and build the confidence to turn an “oh crap” moment into a “we’ve got this” moment.

Prerequisites: Some experience with building trad anchors and trad lead climbing is helpful for this clinic
Required Gear: Personal Gear / Trad Rack, lockers, slings
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Big Wall Bound
sessions.description:
With: Chad Silva, Alpine Endeavors

Have dreams of really big walls? Spend some time with Chad and see what kind of a journey that looks like for an East Coast climber! Chad's got multiple big wall ascents under his belt, and would be stoked to help you get exposure to some of the skills needed to make your way up the big stone, especially when your local training grounds don't offer ideal terrain.

Prerequisites: Trad leaders will get the most out of this class. Ability to top rope belay required

Required Gear: Helmet & Harness, plus any other trad/aid gear you want to get scuffed up
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Bonticou Ecology Tour with a Mohonk Preserve Ranger
sessions.rawName: Bonticou Ecology Tour with a Mohonk Preserve Ranger (Sunday 9am-Noon)
sessions.description:
With: Evan Timony, Mohonk Forestry Specialist and Preserve Ranger

Participate in a 5 mile hike throughout the Mohonk Preserve's Spring Farm area. We will be hiking into the Dwarf Pitch Pines and discussing the Mohonk Preserve's long term monitoring projects, approach to conservation as well the uniqueness that gives this area its character.

We will plan on hiking to the top of Bonticou Crag via the Bonticou Scramble, down the North East Trial with a potential visit to Table Rocks. This will total in mileage around 5 miles and includes a proper scramble, be prepared to use your hands and feet. An alternate route is available around the scramble.

Please note car transportation will be required to access Spring Farm Trailhead, and although it is a short drive carpooling is encouraged.

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: Sturdy hiking shoes, water and snack
sessions.location:
This clinic requires transportation to the Mohonk Preserve Spring farm trailhead and will meet there at 9am.

Location: https://tinyurl.com/mr3rtbub

sessions.name: Climbing Psychology and Mindset Workshop
sessions.description:
Instructor: Jane Bishow-Semevolos, Guide, Genuine Climbing

Join Jane for an incredibly unique journey through the mental planes of climbing.

Elevate your climbing experience by building a stronger, more intentional mindset. Whether your goal is to push higher grades, find flow state more consistently, or simply bring more purpose to your sessions, this workshop will give you the tools to get there.

What We'll Cover:

Key Concepts: Growth mindset, flow state, expanding comfort zones, and understanding motivation.

Practical Tools: Visualization techniques, cultivating curiosity, and actionable goal setting.

What to Expect:
This is an interactive, experiential workshop—not a lecture. Come ready to move, try new approaches, and learn through doing.

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: None
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve visitor center.

sessions.name: Cragside First Aid: Climbing Injuries, Bleeding Control & Improvised Care
sessions.rawName: Cragside First Aid: Climbing Injuries, Bleeding Control & Improvised Care (Sunday 9-1pm)
sessions.description:
Instructors: Raquel Sapp + Brittany Leavitt, Backcountry Pulse

This hands-on clinic focuses on what you can do in those first moments with the skills, people, and equipment around you.

We will work through the traumatic injuries most relevant to climbing falls and accidents, including head and spinal trauma, ankle and lower-extremity injuries, fractures and dislocations, significant bleeding and wounds, and shoulder and upper-extremity injuries.

Rather than focusing on making a perfect diagnosis, we will practice slowing things down enough to notice what matters: what happened, what injuries are most concerning, whether mental or neurologic status is changing, whether circulation and sensation are intact, and what can safely be treated or supported while additional help is on the way.

Participants will practice bleeding control, neurologic and injury assessment, stabilization, and ongoing reassessment. Bring your creative thinking caps! We will explore practical ways to support injuries and improvise care when fully stocked medical kits are not available. We will leave time at the end to strategically plan your personal first aid kit!

Participant Benefit: First Aid Swag!

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: Participants should bring the equipment they would normally have for a day at the crag so that improvisation practice reflects what they actually carry

Suggested items include:
Day-climbing pack
Climbing helmet
Harness
Climbing gear
Extra layer or jacket

Backcountry Pulse will provide medical training equipment and additional scenario and improvisation materials.
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Map and Compass Navigation
sessions.description:
Guide: Gregory Kanter, Gunks Guides

Don’t depend on unreliable apps or a draining phone battery for navigation in the backcountry!

Learn how to expertly navigate the wilderness with our comprehensive Wilderness Navigation Course.

This hands-on course covers essential skills such as reading topographic maps, using a compass for precise orientation, and plotting your own route. Whether you’re hiking familiar trails or venturing off the beaten path into the wilderness, map and compass skills are vital for ensuring safety and confidence.

This half-day wilderness navigation course is perfect for adventurers of all experience levels, from beginners to seasoned explorers. Gain the confidence to navigate the mountains and backcountry with ease and never worry about getting lost again. Sign up today to secure your spot and enhance your outdoor skills!

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: A compass if you have one. Maps and compass will be provided
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Oops, Now What? - Self Rescue for Women & Non-Binary Climbers
sessions.rawName: Oops, Now What? - Self Rescue for Women & Non-Binary Climbers (Sunday 9am-4pm)
sessions.description:
With: Patty Lankhorst, Gunks Guides

Things don’t always go according to plan—but with the right skills, you can handle the unexpected. This hands-on clinic will cover some of the essentials of self-rescue. Possible topics include belay transitions, load transfers, ascending and descending systems, hauling and lowering techniques, and multi-pitch retreats. Learn the “why” behind these systems and build the confidence to problem-solve when things get complicated - with one of the Gunks most celebrated guides.

Note this clinic is only open to women and non-binary climbers.

Prerequisites: To get the most out of this clinic, participants should have experience building trad anchors and leading trad climbs

Required Gear: Personal climbing gear, anything you would normally carry on a day out climbing and leading
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Top Rope Rescue Tactics
sessions.description:
Guide: Teddy Dondaville, Mountain Skills guides

What do you do if something goes wrong during top roping? How do you escape the belay? What if you're belaying from the top? This clinic, led by Teddy Dondanville from Mountain Skills Climbing Guides, will answer these questions and many more. The goal of this clinic will be to each introductory rescue skills and offer best practices to make your top rope practice a little less risky.

Prerequisites: Top rope belaying and climbing experience is preferred
Required Gear: Helmet, harness, climbing shoes. In addition, a selection of belay/rappel devices, slings/ cordelette, friction hitch, lockers, and non-lockers
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Trad Climbing Intensive—A full day introduction to the gear, rope systems, training and ethics of Trad climbing
sessions.rawName: Trad Climbing Intensive—A full day introduction to the gear, rope systems, training and ethics of Trad climbing (Sunday 9-4pm)
sessions.description:
With: Franz Buzawa, Gunks Guides

Welcome to the World of Trad Climbing! Get ready for a full-day, hands-on clinic where the crag is your classroom.

Whether you’re a gym climber, sport climber, or an experienced leader looking to refresh your skills, this clinic will offer a solid foundation for your traditional (aka trad) climbing journey.

The day will be broken up into topic-specific modules covering key concepts such as active and passive protection, gear-based anchor building, rope system transitions, training strategies, ethics, and more.

Expect a practical, information-rich experience—bring your questions, your curiosity, and a notebook!

Prerequisites: The clinic is designed for climbers from diverse backgrounds and levels of experience, however prior experience with belaying, both top-rope and lead as well as rappelling is extremely useful

Required Gear: Helmet, harness, ATC-style belay device, ABD-style belay device, preferably a Grigri, several, up to 6, locking carabiners (similar to Petzl Attaché), at least 1 double-length (48″ or 120 cm) sling, 2 shoulder-length (24″ or 60 cm) slings, other personal gear that you use or have questions about
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: How Trusty are those Rusties?
sessions.description:
Instructor: Richard Goldstone

Clip-and-whip or just plain skip? Or maybe time to tie-off?

Learn about the intricacies and history of iron, and how trustworthy exactly it can and cannot be. Chances are you have encountered an original piece of fixed hardware, if you have wondered the vintage then this class is for you.

This clinic presents some of the history of piton development, discusses appropriate attitudes and practices for dealing with in-situ gear, and describes selection, placing and removal (in the context of free climbing—this is not an aid tutorial).

This clinic meets at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center and will be held in the visitor center classroom.
sessions.location: MP Visitor Center Classroom

sessions.name: Safe Rappelling Practices
sessions.description:
Guide: Angelo Urrico, Rise Outside guides

Join Angelo to learn techniques for safely descending single or multiple rappels, using the gear that you are comfortable with. You will also learn several methods for keeping your less experienced partner safe on rappel.

Prerequisites: Previous outdoor rock climbing experience; a desire to improve safety on descent for yourself and your partner
Required gear: Personal climbing kit, rappel equipment
sessions.location: Meet at the afternoon clinic meeting location.

sessions.name: Climbing Photography Masterclass
sessions.description:
Guide: Chris Vultaggio

Want to take your climbing photography to the next level?

Join professional climbing photographer Chris Vultaggio to cover everything from lens choices to lighting, composition to fixed-line logistics.

Time permitting, we will be able to practice some rope ascending for some hands-on skill development.

Prerequisites: Photography and climbing knowledge a plus, especially experience and confidence in rappelling and anchors
Required Gear: Personal climbing kit, camera kit, rope ascending kit if you have one
sessions.location: Meet at Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center.

sessions.name: Half Rope Usage: Techniques, Pros, and Cons
sessions.rawName: Half Rope Usage: Techniques, Pros, and Cons (Sunday 1pm-3pm)
sessions.description:
Instructor: Richard Goldstone
You're finishing out your route, top of the cliff within a few body-lengths. Your partner is out of sight, under a roof and a long traverse back to the belay.

Each step becomes more tedious like you're dragging an elephant from your harness - and you find yourself yarding up armloads of slack just to move. We've all been there, but did you know there is an easy fix?

Half ropes are not popular except in the UK, where they are the technique of choice for trad, and for good reason with their wandering pitches - just like someplace else we know...

Everyone knows they have the potential to reduce friction, but is that the whole story? Do the Brits know something we don’t?

As a 30+ year user, Dr. Goldstone will share his insights on how this seasoned practice applies in the Gunks, both pros and cons.

This clinic will meet at the Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center and be held in the visitor center classroom.
sessions.location: Mohonk Preserve Visitor Center Classroom

sessions.name: Multipitching in Party of Three
sessions.description:
Guide: Teddy Dondaville, Mountain Skills guides

Climbing in a party of three can be cumbersome– there’s a lot of rope to manage and an extra person. This clinic, led by Teddy Dondanville from Mountain Skills Climbing Guides, will teach best practices for climbing in a party of three, including a deep dive into two belay methods. In addition, this clinic will offer some efficiency hacks to make the process more smoother.

Prerequisites: Lead multi-pitch experience. (This workshop will be taught through the perspective of the leader.)
Required Gear: Standard multi pitch kit, including a harness, a selection of belay/rappel devices, lockers, non-lockers, slings or PAS, anchor building material
sessions.location: This clinic meets at the afternoon clinic meetup location.

sessions.name: Wilderness Survival for the Outdoor Recreator
sessions.rawName: Wilderness Survival for the Outdoor Recreator (Sunday 2pm-6pm)
sessions.description:
Guide: Gregory Kanter, Gunks Guides

Ready to become more “outdoorsy?"

Whether you’re a beginner looking to start your outdoor journey or an experienced adventurer seeking a skills refresh, Wilderness Survival is the perfect course for you! Learn how to thrive in the wilderness with the right preparation, gear, clothing, and skills to manage risks and ensure comfort on all your outdoor adventures.

In this comprehensive wilderness survival course, we’ll cover essential topics like the Ten Essentials, clothing layering techniques, dealing with environmental threats and weather, animal encounters, medical considerations, and effective decision-making in the backcountry.

To cap off the day, we’ll engage in role-playing scenarios to put your newly acquired skills to the test and boost your confidence.

This course is ideal for outdoor enthusiasts of all experience levels, offering practical skills for anyone who wants to explore the wilderness safely and confidently. Sign up today to enhance your outdoor recreation knowledge and wilderness survival abilities!

Prerequisites: None
Required Gear: Just your clothing you’d be wearing for a day out and a pack you’d normally carry
sessions.location: Meet at afternoon clinic meeting location.

sessions.name: The First 30 Minutes: Climbing Scenario Lab & SAR Handoff
sessions.rawName: The First 30 Minutes: Climbing Scenario Lab & SAR Handoff (Monday 9am-1pm)
sessions.description:
Instructors: Raquel Sapp + Brittany Leavitt, Backcountry Pulse

Part III in our inaugural Climbing First Aid series, led by the amazing team at Backcountry Pulse!

The first few minutes after a climbing accident rarely feel organized. There may be several people trying to help, incomplete information, an injured partner who is scared or in pain, and no obvious answer to what should happen first.

This workshop is a chance to practice that part before you ever have to do it for real.

Working in small groups, participants will respond to realistic climbing accident scenarios informed by incident patterns reported in the Gunks and Accidents in North American Climbing. Scenarios may involve a leader fall with head trauma, a significant lower-extremity injury, or a fall with possible spinal or neurologic concerns.

Rather than being told exactly what to do, each group will work through the situation together: assessing the scene and patient, identifying priorities, providing initial care, using the people and resources available, activating help, communicating location and patient information, and continuing to reassess as the situation changes.

Throughout the scenarios, participants will document patient information, assessments, treatments, vital signs, and changes over time. Each scenario ends with an often-overlooked part of climbing emergency response: organizing what you know and providing a clear, useful patient handoff to Search and Rescue so the next team can build on the care already underway.

Participant Benefit: Rescue Ally App - Everyone who participates in The First 30 Minutes will receive an exclusive workshop offer for lifetime access to Rescue Ally for $25, a $75 value!

Prerequisites: None. However, it is best suited for participants with some wilderness medicine training/experience

Required Gear:

Participants should bring:
Day-climbing pack
Climbing helmet
Harness
Smartphone with Rescue Ally free trial downloaded
Climbing Gear
Extra layer or jacket

Backcountry Pulse will provide all equipment, medical training materials, and scenario supplies.
sessions.location: New Paltz, NY

Join us for vendors, contests, and films starting at 5PM!

Saturday night Keynote speaker: Jonna Bragg.

Doors – 5pm
Jonna Bragg 7pm
Films 8pm

Our keynote presenter will be Jonna Bragg, historic Gunks first ascensionist of such groundbreaking lines as Fat City Direct, Kansas City, Gravity’s Rainbow, Enduro Man, Erect Direction, and more.

Not to mention her 1976 legendary first ascent of Patagonia’s towering Torre Egger.

Bragg has been counted among the world’s best climbers of the 1970s, as one quarter of the dream team of her, John Stannard, Henry Barber, and Steve Wunsch.

Come hear her tales of what it took to push grades into the hard 5.11-12 range, then get psyched for our feature film presentation: The Queen Swing.
